mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede economic slowdowns, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate contracting consumer demand, reducing corporate earnings expectations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening economic momentum, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle expansions when INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer confidence and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during demand expansion cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST rises.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 207.0 signals persistent inflation, prompting restrictive monetary policy that causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 207.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate monetary tightening coinciding with labor market weakness, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE rises.

mechanism_narrative: During labor market tightening cycles, a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals weakening economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during labor market tightening when PAYEMS declines.
